title: Semantic Tokens Architecture
summary: Derive catalogue-token syntax and family/target data from the accepted discovery, creation, and editing workflow.
content_html:
Semantic Tokens Architecture

Outcome

Provide one manage-only Docs Viewer extension path from a registered token family to source-editor authoring, current-buffer inspection, local rendering, generated relationships, and a focused report.

The accepted Source Editor UI is the input to this architecture. It first determines when an author searches, compares, selects, and locks a target. Token syntax records that decision. The token-definition registry selects the configured workflow and target projection. Generated data records actual document usage.

Token Syntax

CT-P0 accepts this deterministic source form:

[[<family>:<target-type>:<canonical-id>|<escaped-title>]]

The first accepted examples are:

[[catalogue:work:00638|3 symbols]]
[[catalogue:work:00008|nerve]]
[[catalogue:series:105|nerve]]
[[catalogue:moment:d-20260215-000000-02a1a4|13 moments in october]]

Family and target-type keys are lower-case identifiers matching [a-z][a-z0-9-]*. A lexical id matches [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*; its accepted canonical form is then owned by the target-type id policy. Catalogue Work uses five digits, while Series and Moment use lower-case alphanumeric-and-hyphen ids. The modal may normalize accepted input, but serialization always records the canonical id.

Title is a required, single-line occurrence field. The modal trims its outer whitespace before serialization and preserves its remaining Unicode text. The serializer escapes backslash, pipe, and closing bracket as \\, \|, and \], in that order. The parser decodes only those three escapes; an unknown escape, an empty Title, an invalid identity component, or an unterminated token is malformed. Identity components are never escaped.

Serialization emits no optional whitespace around separators. Parsing returns the raw token and a zero-based half-open [start, end) source range. Inline code, fenced code, and HTML comments are inactive. A collapsed caret activates a supported occurrence only when start < caret < end; a shared boundary between adjacent tokens activates neither. Malformed and unsupported kinds never activate a token.

The immutable identity is (family, target type, target id). The author need not choose the type before searching; selecting a result supplies it. The displayed Title remains occurrence metadata and does not edit the canonical target.

The versioned shared contract fixture is docs-viewer/tests/fixtures/semantic_tokens_catalogue_v1.json. Python and browser implementations must consume its same raw strings, decoded fields, ranges, inactive contexts, and caret expectations rather than maintaining separate examples.

Authoring Validation And Tolerant Build

The add-token modal is the only semantic validation owner. At confirmation it:

  • requires a target selected from the current family lookup;
  • normalizes and validates the concrete identity;
  • validates required occurrence fields;
  • serializes the accepted syntax deterministically.

This validates the new string being inserted, not the whole document. Markdown source remains directly user-editable before or after insertion.

The builder is a tolerant projector, not a semantic validator. It may recognize a syntactically plausible string and attempt to resolve its identity. It emits a link and usage-index occurrence only when the configured target lookup returns a safe, workable destination. Otherwise it:

  • leaves the original source substring unchanged for ordinary Markdown rendering;
  • emits no semantic link;
  • emits no usage or reverse-relationship row;
  • does not warn or fail the document build.

This applies to malformed syntax, unsupported token kinds, missing identities, and lookup results without a usable destination. Grammar recognition and best-effort resolution are implementation steps, not validation outcomes. The normal build records no broken-link result; the separate read-only audit owns diagnosis.

Token-Definition Registry

Proposed checked-in location:

docs-viewer/config/semantic-tokens/families.json

Use a schema-versioned envelope with one record per accepted family. A family and target-type pair forms one token-kind definition, such as catalogue:work. The registry is checked-in configuration describing supported token kinds; it is not a collection of tokens found in documents and it does not contain canonical target records.

A family record defines:

  • stable family key and author-facing action name;
  • required and optional occurrence fields;
  • occurrence fields the Info view may edit;
  • add-action, modal, and Info-view contribution ids;
  • generated relationship and report meaning.

Each accepted target type within the family defines:

  • stable type key and author-facing result label;
  • canonical owner and target-lookup adapter;
  • immutable id field plus modal-time normalization and validation;
  • distinguishing result metadata and optional preview data;
  • projection adapter id and the named fields it supplies;
  • the presentation type and destination for each projected field.

The Catalogue family initially declares Work, Series, and Moment. Its discovery adapter returns them in one result set; optional filters narrow that set without requiring a type choice before search.

The registry selects declared capabilities. Parser, normalizer, resolver, and UI implementations remain code-owned; JSON must not become an executable plugin framework.

Configured Target Projection

An individual token resolves its identity through its token-kind definition. It does not receive a canonical record and interpret that record itself:

token occurrence: catalogue:work + 00008
    -> catalogue:work definition
    -> configured Work projection adapter
    -> named projection fields
    -> add modal, Info view, renderer, or report

The definition declares the projection interface. Its adapter owns canonical data access, array selection, URL construction, and other domain logic. For example, a Work token need not inspect series_ids[] or downloads[]. If the definition exposes url, media, or file, the adapter supplies those named values according to the Work contract and the consuming UI simply reads or displays them.

A definition may deliberately expose a list, but canonical arrays are not implicitly projected and a token never traverses arbitrary canonical JSON. Changing the canonical storage shape therefore affects the focused adapter, not token syntax or every token consumer.

Metadata Sources

Use metadata only with its source qualified. The Info panel can combine values from different places, but those places do not have the same authority or freshness:

qualified term stored where access path Info-panel use
token identity and occurrence fields current Markdown source parse the current editor buffer identity is read-only; declared occurrence fields are editable
usage-index attributes generated semantic-token usage JSON match the rebuilt occurrence optional read-only context; never overrides the current buffer
canonical target fields target owner, such as the Work record target adapter only not read directly by the Info panel
target-lookup projection fields generated lookup or focused adapter result keyed by target identity token-kind lookup contract declared read-only context, destinations, and previews

Field authority and delivery source are separate questions. An occurrence field may be repeated in the usage index, while a canonical or derived target field may be materialized in the target lookup. Those copies do not acquire authority from the JSON file that happens to deliver them.

The usage index may denormalize useful attributes for reports or the Info panel, but it represents the last rebuild and is not the source of truth for an unsaved active occurrence. A target field is not available merely because some usage JSON contains a similarly named value.

For example, files[] remains canonical Work data. Showing a file, file count, or selected download requires a declared catalogue:work lookup projection whose adapter reads the Work record and supplies the agreed shape. A preview image follows the same lookup path: work_id selects a Work lookup row or focused result containing the declared preview projection. Neither the token nor the usage index discovers the preview by traversing Work media fields.

Field Authority

Each family/target-type definition must classify its fields before deciding which values appear in source tokens, canonical JSON, generated lookup data, or the Info panel:

field class authority token storage Info-panel behavior
identity selected concrete target required and immutable read-only
occurrence this use in this document stored when set editable when declared
canonical target existing domain owner never copied into the token read-only projection
derived resolver using identity, occurrence context, and canonical data never stored as a full derived value read-only projection

The token-kind definition declares field names, types, source class, required state, whether an occurrence field is editable, and which named target projections may be displayed. It does not become the value owner for canonical target fields.

Work Example

For Work 00008:

field class treatment
work_id: "00008" identity store in the token and never edit in the Info view
canonical title, series_ids, downloads, and media source/version fields canonical target remain behind the Studio Work projection adapter; the token does not inspect them
series_id: "105" used to open the Work within one Series occurrence context store only when that contextual destination is chosen; validate against canonical membership
url derived projection adapter resolves it from Work identity plus optional Series context
media derived projection adapter supplies the configured media representation
file derived projection adapter selects the configured canonical download representation; the token does not resolve downloads[]
displayed Title occurrence store in the token and allow editing

The current nerve Work belongs to both Series 105 and 026. That makes a singular Series choice occurrence context, not a copied canonical Work field. Changing that context may change the destination without changing Work identity.

Tag Example

For a future Tag family:

field class treatment
tag_id, such as domain:nerve identity store in the token and keep immutable
group, label, and description canonical target remain with the Studio Tag owner and are exposed only when declared by the Tag projection
associated sub-scope data_doc canonical target relationship if it is the same for every use add to the canonical Tag owner or a focused canonical Tag-to-document mapping, then expose it through the Tag projection
displayed Title or usage-specific relation metadata occurrence store in the token and expose through the Tag Info view
detail URL derived resolve from the canonical document relationship and route contract

If a new field describes the target everywhere, extend its canonical owner and the token-kind lookup projection only when a consumer needs it. If it describes only this document occurrence, extend the token-kind field schema and source syntax. If it is computable, extend the projection adapter. Generated lookup and usage JSON may denormalize values for use, but remains reproducible and non-authoritative.

Adding an optional occurrence field should require only a declared field schema, syntax/parser support, a supported Info-panel control type, and focused fixtures. Complex fields or new canonical ownership still require a specific design; an arbitrary JSON property must not silently become editable UI.

Generated Lookup And Usage Data

Accepted working locations:

docs-viewer/data/generated/semantic-tokens/target-lookup.json
docs-viewer/scopes/<scope>/published/documents/semantic-tokens/index.json

Each lookup row includes family, target type, id, title, and the compact declared projection needed for discovery or Info-panel context. That projection may include a preview image. The Catalogue lookup combines Work, Series, and Moment rows without exposing their raw canonical records.

The per-scope file is the derived token usage index: what resolved token occurrences are actually present in documents. It is reproducible local manage data, not a registry, canonical target store, or public projection. Each row needs catalogue target type/id, occurrence title, source document, and resolved target. Ignored token-like strings do not enter this index.

There are no per-document or per-target usage payloads. Targeted builds preserve untouched occurrences by grouping the existing scope index by source document. Any future document- or target-specific projection requires a concrete consumer.

The manage-only Semantic Tokens report reads the selected scope's usage index, shows occurrence Title and concrete identity, and resolves its source document against that scope's index tree to provide the managed document link.

Broken-Link Audit And Repair

Keep failure diagnosis in the existing Docs Broken Links audit and report. The separate manage-only Semantic Tokens Report is an inventory of resolved usage-index occurrences; it does not diagnose unresolved source.

The semantic-token audit is an explicit, read-only management action. It scans source Markdown with the accepted token parser because unresolved occurrences are deliberately absent from the generated usage index. For each identifiable token-like occurrence, it uses the token-definition registry and target lookup to report at least:

  • unsupported token kind;
  • missing target identity;
  • resolved target without a safe, workable destination.

A result includes source scope/document, raw token text, parsed family/type/identity where available, failure reason, and enough source location to return to the occurrence. Conservatively identifiable malformed syntax may be included, but arbitrary bracketed prose must not be classified as a token.

Repair is user-controlled:

run Docs Broken Links audit
    -> open owning document in source mode
    -> select broken occurrence where possible
    -> Remove token
    -> Add <family> token through the validated modal
    -> rebuild
    -> rerun audit

The audit never writes source, retargets an occurrence, blocks save/rebuild, or adds broken occurrences to the usage index. An unavailable target can also require repair in its canonical owner or projection adapter rather than a source edit; the report exposes the reason without choosing that repair.

Native, Generated, And Published

Apply the repository Projection Contract:

role semantic-token example authority or purpose
checked configuration token-kind definitions declares supported capability; not content
native or canonical source Markdown token occurrences and canonical Work, Series, Moment, or Tag records editable source of truth in the owning domain
built/generated working data manage target lookup and usage index reproducible enrichment, authoring, and resolved relationship input
published public projection resolved ordinary anchors in eligible document payloads browser-safe rendered content with no public token-data dependency

Generated describes how an artifact is produced; published describes an intended consumer. A public payload is therefore generated too, but it is not the manage lookup or usage index copied into a public directory.

Public document projection resolves supported tokens during the ordinary build:

canonical document + resolvable token occurrences + focused target lookup
    -> build-time token resolution
    -> ordinary document HTML anchor
    -> public reader

The anchor may retain inert data-semantic-token-* attributes, but the public reader does not consult the token-definition registry, canonical source, manage target lookup, or local usage index. The usage index remains local generated data and the publish gate omits its directory.

Ownership

responsibility owner
canonical Work, Series, Moment, and later target records existing domain owners
supported family and target-type definitions integrated Docs Viewer token-definition registry
manage-safe target lookup focused generator and generated lookup
named target projections code-owned adapter selected by each token-kind definition
token grammar shared contract with Python and browser conformance fixtures
source selection and buffer mutation generic source-editor adapter
family actions, modals, detection, and Info views manage-only semantic-token feature
rebuild parsing and usage-index generation Docs Viewer builder semantic-token owner
resolved usage occurrences per-scope generated semantic-token index
resolved-token inventory and owning-document links manage-only Semantic Tokens report
broken-token diagnosis and source repair handoff existing manage-only Docs Broken Links service and report

Use registry only for token-definition configuration. Use usage index for the generated inventory of occurrences in documents. Catalogue is one semantic and UI family with Work, Series, and Moment token kinds. Their target records remain with their current domain owners. Tag is a separate future family.

Wiring

Catalogue token-kind definitions + projection adapters
    -> combined Work/Series/Moment lookup
    -> Add catalogue token toolbar action
    -> discovery and required-data modal
    -> selected concrete target type + id
    -> catalogue token serialization
    -> source-editor range replacement
    -> current-buffer token parser
    -> Catalogue Info-panel view
    -> normal Rebuild doc
    -> builder parsing + generated usage index
    -> manage-only Semantic Tokens report

source Markdown
    -> explicit Docs Broken Links audit
    -> semantic-token issue row
    -> source-editor repair workflow

Insertion, update, and removal change only the local source buffer. The normal source-editor workflow remains the sole write and rebuild owner.

Target identity has one UI owner at each stage:

  • before insertion, the family-specific modal owns target lookup and selection;
  • after insertion, the parsed token owns identity and the Info view receives it as read-only context.

The Info panel does not reload the target picker to change an identity. This keeps creation validation inside one modal transaction and prevents occurrence editing from becoming an implicit re-targeting workflow. It may still perform a read-only lookup for the existing identity to obtain declared preview or target context.

UI-Driven Refactoring Gate

CT-P1 resolved the creation pressures:

  • the source adapter now exposes current-buffer revision, captured selection, and guarded captured-range replacement;
  • generic main-view action and source-action-state contributions allow Catalogue to register its toolbar action without a family branch in the source-editor lifecycle;
  • the pilot mixed-target result list is rehosted in the Catalogue add modal, and the fixed source-mode Info picker is retired.

P2 completed exact-range guarded update/removal, contextual Info routing, and the accepted parser and token-definition registry.

The remaining presentation and conformance constraints still apply:

  • The native textarea can highlight one active token with setSelectionRange; persistent syntax decoration is not required for the first delivery.
  • Python and browser parsers cannot share implementation code, so shared grammar fixtures must prove identical occurrence and boundary behavior.

If existing hosted-view or exact-range extension points cannot meet the P2 contracts cleanly, refactor the generic plumbing first within the Catalogue delivery. Do not move token knowledge into core to avoid that refactor.

Pilot Disposition

CT-P3 removed the parallel pilot registry, parser, generated paths, report loader, read endpoints, Info picker, tests, and public copies. The reusable mixed-target behavior now belongs to the Catalogue modal; local relationships use the accepted semantic-tokens contracts; Docs Broken Links owns diagnosis; and the active 3 symbols occurrence uses Catalogue syntax. No compatibility path, registry alias, route-only unresolved link, or public relationship replacement remains.

Boundaries

  • No token-definition registry, family list, or token-specific view in generic core.
  • No source-save or rebuild target-existence gate.
  • No service endpoint solely for token lookup or editing.
  • No public token-definition registry, manage usage index, token-resolution runtime, or report in this delivery.
  • No automatic semantic wrapping of ordinary links, images, or files.
  • No executable directives, generic graph, background crawler, or continuous reconciliation service.
